oct_29: 1965: The Who release "My Generation" in the UK.
1971: Duane Allman dies in a motorcycle crash.
Birthdays: Peter Green (Fleetwood Mac, 1946), Roger O'Donnell (The Cure, 1955), Peter Timmins (Cowboy Junkies, 1965).
oct_30: 1968: Marvin Gaye's "I Heard It Through the Grapevine" reaches No. 1 on the Hot 100.
1971: John Lennon's Imagine tops the UK chart.
1998: All four original members of Black Sabbath reunite on Letterman to play "Paranoid".
Birthdays: Grace Slick (Jefferson Airplane, 1939), Gavin Rossdale (Bush, 1967).
1938: Orson Welles' War of the Worlds airs on CBS (Mercury Theatre on the Air, 8 p.m. ET).
2026: Queens of the Stone Age, Perfecth (Matador), Ministry, Hate to Go (Cleopatra) and Mitski, Puberty 2 10th Anniversary Edition (Dead Oceans) are out.
today_in_music.fits: O'Donnell's birthday fits The Cure "Lullaby" (Set 3). The Sabbath reunion fits Black Sabbath "Black Sabbath" (Set 3).
today_in_music.source: thisdayinmusic.com Oct. 29 and 30; Wikipedia and History.com (War of the Worlds); Matador, Side-Line (releases)

opening: Halloween show. Punk and post-punk focus, week 3 of 4: goth and post-punk tonight. D.C. hardcore Nov. 5.
Tonight: Ministry, Misfits, The Cramps, Siouxsie, Joy Division, then a Queens of the Stone Age Triple Shot to open Hour 2.
Reviewed albums in rotation: one track each from 13 albums, spread through both hours.
after_set_1: Screamin' Jay Hawkins recorded I Put a Spell on You in 1956. Misfits released Halloween as a single in 1981. The Cramps' Goo Goo Muck is from Psychedelic Jungle (1981).
The Lemonheads released a 12-inch of Roky, with The Bevis Frond, on Oct. 16 on Fire Records. Roky Erickson's I Walked with a Zombie is from 1981.
Ministry's final album, Hate to Go (Take Out or Delivery), is out Fri. Oct. 30 on Cleopatra. Closing track features former bassist Paul Barker. Farewell tour starts April 2, 2027 in Utrecht.
end_hour_1: Joy Division, Siouxsie and The Cure tonight. Roger O'Donnell of The Cure was born Oct. 29, 1955.
Public Image Ltd. released Death Disco in July 1979. YouTube Music lists the studio cut as Swan Lake.
Station ID at the top of the hour.
triple_shot_intro: Thursday Triple Shot: Queens of the Stone Age. Perfecth, the band's ninth album, is out Fri. Oct. 30 on Matador. Josh Homme and Michael Shuman produced it.
Where the Goth Girls At? is the new single. No One Knows is from Songs for the Deaf (2002). Burn the Witch is from Lullabies to Paralyze (2005).
after_triple_shot: On Oct. 30, 1938, CBS aired Orson Welles' War of the Worlds on The Mercury Theatre on the Air. The FCC investigated afterward and found no law was broken.
bay_area_break: Tonight: Bottom of the Hill tribute night, a Halloween covers show at Kilowatt, Katie Pruitt at Chapel.

Fri. Oct. 30: Cold Cave, SRSQ and Houses of Heaven at Great American Music Hall. Sat. Oct. 31: Halloween tribute bands at Thee Stork Club and Rocky Horror with a live cast at the UC Theater in Berkeley. Sun. Nov. 1: Frankie And The Witch Fingers at Great American Music Hall.
anniversary: Mitski's Puberty 2 turns 10. The 10th Anniversary Edition is out Fri. Oct. 30 on Dead Oceans.
Fake Names released Punk Ruins today (Oct. 23) on Epitaph. Recorded in five days at Electrical Audio in Chicago.
Black Sabbath: the four original members reunited on Letterman Oct. 30, 1998 (verify).
closing: Next week, Nov. 5: US hardcore and Washington D.C. Fugazi, Husker Du, Bad Brains, short songs.
